### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

but by the uncertain will of the Divine Power <note>original: *Numinis*</note>. Therefore, to seek out the causes of these matters is a doubtful task; nor would you necessarily reach a conclusion. If, then, the distinction between clean and unclean living creatures was known in the age of Noah; if that distinction pertained to sacrifices; and if, finally, the same was established by God; it follows that the use of sacrifices had already been ordained by God before the flood.

XV. Nor do I see what can be objected, unless someone has set their mind to contend with Spencer <note>John Spencer (1630–1693), an influential English theologian who argued that many Hebrew rituals were adapted from Egyptian customs</note> that Moses, when writing to those to whom the Law was already known, made mention of clean and unclean animals in the history of the flood by way of anticipation <term>prolepsis: a literary device where a future event or condition is described as if it has already occurred at an earlier time</term> <note>original: *κατά πρόληψιν* (kata prolepsin)</note>. But such a fiction of anticipation, since it usually proceeds from prejudices drawn from elsewhere, ought deservedly to be suspected; especially if it is destitute of foundation and does violence to the text. Both are the case here. For what even minimal sign reveals itself here that would cause a suspicion of anticipation? I hear Spencer saying (*Book I. Chapter v. Section 1.*) that it is beyond all belief that God would want to burden Noah and his descendants with institutions of this kind, which would be of no use at that time. But this itself is what is disputed, not an argument for determining the controversy. I add that this fabricated anticipation does violence to the text. God says to Noah, "From all clean cattle take for yourself seven pairs, from the unclean, two." Noah obeyed the command, and receiving those coming to him, both clean and unclean in the established number, he took them into the ark. When the flood was finished, he offered burnt offerings to God from all clean cattle as well as birds. Who here, unless captured by an ill-advised love of anticipation, would dare to maintain that God gave no instruction regarding the distinction of animals, or that Noah did not understand it, when the clear language of the history seems to be written with the clarity of sunbeams? Let us suppose that God proposed to Noah all the species of living things not under the title of "clean" or "unclean"—though the words of the History say otherwise—but by their own distinct names: yet this certainly cannot be denied or called into doubt, that Noah knew those living things of which he had seven pairs in the Ark were accepted by God for sacrifices, and the others were not. For he did not adopt this distinction by chance or without consideration.

<margin>XVI. Jewish trifles regarding the bull which Adam offered.</margin>
XVI. And let these things now suffice for our discussion regarding the first origin of sacrifices. For the trifles that the Jewish Masters babble about a bull offered by Adam, which was equipped with a single horn, and whose horn emerged from the mother earth before its feet when it was brought forth, are unworthy of our mention. If you were to try to elicit mysteries from these things, you would only produce greater trifles. However, for those who take pleasure in not being ignorant of them, let them consult *Bochart*, in the *Hierozoicon* <note>A famous 17th-century work on the animals of the Bible by Samuel Bochart</note> *Book III. Chapter XXVI. page 944.*

### ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND CHRIST.

<margin>XVII. *Lightfoot's* ingenious commentary on *Genesis* 4:7.</margin>
XVII. Somewhat more plausible is the commentary of *Lightfoot* <note>John Lightfoot (1602–1675) was an English clergyman and Hebrew scholar known for using Rabbinic literature to explain the Bible.</note> on that speech with which God addresses Cain in *Genesis* 4:7: *If you do well, will you not be accepted? But if you do not do well,* "sin," that is, a victim for expiating sin, "lies before the doors." <note>original: *חטאת רבץ* (chatat rovetz). Lightfoot argued the Hebrew word 'chatat' here refers to a 'sin offering' rather than the act of sin itself.</note> It is as if God wished to say: provided you repent for your evil counsel, there is no reason to lose heart; a sacrificial victim is ready at hand, by the offering of which, joined with repentance, you may obtain pardon. <margin>*Add to the Preface, §. XXV*</margin> Thus, just as God had proposed the first announcement of faith to Adam in the promise of Christ (*Genesis* 3:15), he proposed to Cain the announcement of repentance, along with the doctrine of expiatory sacrifices. However, even this explanation is subject to many objections; and it departs so far from the received interpretation that I would not dare to sell it as a solid argument. Let those points suffice which were established with considerably more firmness in the preceding sections.

<margin>XVIII. In the beginning, the right of sacrificing was restricted to no specific order.</margin>
XVIII. Let us now begin another chapter: let us inquire, **TO WHOM THE RIGHT OF SACRIFICING FORMERLY BELONGED.** Regarding this matter, I hold the following view. From the most ancient times, it was lawful for anyone to perform their own *private* sacred rites: a fact which the history of *Cain* and *Abel* proves. For those who dictate that both brothers brought the sacrifices intended for God to Adam, to be properly offered up by him, offer no suitable reason why they say so. Indeed, the history itself sufficiently teaches that the father was not present at those sacrifices; otherwise, his authority could have settled the quarrel between the brothers. It is believable that domestic sacred rites were performed by him who was the head of the family. By that same right, *Noah*, *Jacob*, and *Job* sacrificed each for his own family (*Genesis* 8:20; 35:3; *Job* 1:5). After larger assemblies from many families merged into a whole people, and sacrifices began to be offered for the entire people, the right of sacrificing was in the power of the leader of the assembly, should he wish it. Thus *Melchizedek* was both King and Priest at the same time. And by the same right, *Moses* moistened the altar with that blood by which the Israelite covenant was sanctioned (*Exodus* 24:8). In this sacred rite, he was assisted by "youths," or *the young men of the children of Israel, who offered burnt offerings and sacrificed peace offerings to the Lord* (ibid, verse 5). Such men are called "the priests who approach the Lord" <note>original: *הכהנים הנגשים אל יהוה* (ha-kohanim ha-neggashim el Yehovah)</note> in *Exodus* 19:22. Nevertheless, it does not appear from these instances that the duty of sacrificing had been restricted up to this point to any certain order or specific persons by a special institution of God.

<margin>XIX. Connection to the prerogatives of the Firstborn.</margin>
XIX. For as to the fact that many men, even the most learned, have believed along with the Jews that the priestly dignity belonged to the prerogatives of the firstborn, *Outram* (*On Sacrifices, Book 1, Chapter 4*) <note>William Outram (1626–1679) was an English theologian whose work 'De Sacrificiis' is a classic study of the sacrificial system.</note> and *Owen* (*On the Epistle to the Hebrews, Vol. 2, p. 156 and following*) <note>John Owen (1616–1683) was a leading Puritan theologian and Vice-Chancellor of Oxford University.</note> have demonstrated that this is established by no solid argument—indeed, that it is destroyed by many examples. I also, according to my

# BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

...I had formerly collected a great many things pertaining to this matter, but since that most learned man, *Campegius Vitringa*, <note>Campegius Vitringa (1659–1722) was a prominent Dutch theologian and Hebraist known for his commentary on Isaiah.</note> has now taken it up in a copious and elegant dissertation which appears in his *Sacred Observations, Book II, Chapters II and III*, let the fair and noble reader allow himself to be referred there. There, unless I am mistaken, the reader will find himself freed from all the prejudices that common opinion has produced.

<margin>XX. This liberty is a figure of a broader liberty.</margin>
XX. Nor is this ancient liberty of sacrificing unworthy of our observation, since it leads our thoughts to the most happy times of the New Testament. In those times, it is granted to all the faithful without distinction to be Kings and Priests to God (*Revelation 1:6*) for the purpose of offering *spiritual sacrifices to God through Jesus Christ (1 Peter 2:5).*

<margin>XXI. Promised through Isaiah.</margin>
XXI. *Isaiah* prophesied magnificently concerning this remarkable blessing in *Chapter 56:3, 4, 5*:
> *Let not the foreigner who joins himself to the Lord speak, saying, “The Lord has utterly separated me from His people”; nor let the eunuch say, “Behold, I am a dry tree.” For thus says the Lord concerning the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, and choose what pleases me, and take hold of my covenant: I will give to them in my house, and within my walls, a <term>place and a name</term> <note>original: "יד ושם" (Yad Vashem). Literally "a hand and a name," signifying a monument or a place of memorial.</note> better than that of sons; I will give to each of them an everlasting name that shall not be cut off.*

To understand these things, it must be observed that certain foreigners, and especially eunuchs, were excluded by the <term>Mosaic Law</term> <note>The body of laws traditionally attributed to Moses in the first five books of the Bible.</note> from the congregation of the Lord and from all the privileges of the Israelite people (*Deuteronomy 23:1, 2, 3*). From this arose a significant cause for their complaint. God removes this through this most excellent promise, pledging that in the future they would enjoy not only the privileges of the people, but even the prerogatives of the Levites and Priests. Every Israelite had a *place and a name in the land of Canaan*. For Joshua, in the distribution of the land, recorded the names of the heads of each family in a register, and assigned to each name its own *space* for dwelling and possession. However, no certain inheritance was assigned to the Levites: *the Lord was the portion of their inheritance*. This was especially true of the Priests. Their names and classes were inscribed in the temple, where a space for staying was granted to them in the chambers around the temple and its courts. And these very things, which were once private to the Priests, God promises to the eunuchs—that is, to those who seemed most removed from all dignity among his people, and especially from the Priesthood.

<margin>XXII. From Jeremiah</margin>
XXII. To the same point belongs the no less famous oracle of *Jeremiah*, also examined by us elsewhere (*Chapter 31:12, 14*):
> *Those who come shall sing on the Height of Zion, and shall flow together to the goodness of the Lord, to the grain, and the wine, and the oil, to the young of the flock and the herd; and their soul shall be like a watered garden, and they shall no longer sorrow. And I will saturate the soul...*

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND CHRIST.

...*the soul of the Priests with fatness, and my people shall be satisfied with my goodness, says Jehovah.* <note>The author is quoting Jeremiah 31:14, which describes the spiritual and physical abundance God promises to His people.</note> The Temple was built on *Zion*. The Temple itself was higher than the other parts of *Zion*. In the Temple, the *Sanctuary* was higher than the *Courts*. But the *Holy of Holies* <note>original: *Sanctum Sanctorum*</note> was the highest of all. It was forbidden for common *Israelites* to intrude further than the *courts*. Only the *Priests* were permitted to enter the *Sanctuary*, and only the single *High Priest* <note>original: *Pontifici*</note> could set foot in the *Holy of Holies*. Furthermore, those things which were brought to *Zion* and did not belong to the *Altar* were the property of the *Priests*; because they were consecrated to the *Lord*, they were called the *Lord’s goods*. But here it is foretold that in the future, when the ransom has been paid, *Israel* redeemed, and delivered from the hand of the stronger, the way shall lie open to anyone. It will be permitted for all indiscriminately to come not only to *Zion*, but even to the *Height of Zion*, and there to shout for joy because of the salvation obtained. No height shall be excluded; there they may enjoy the preeminences of the *Priests* and enjoy in abundance those goods which *God* bestows from his inexhaustible goodness upon his intimate friends: *not even the fatness being removed, which he formerly reserved for his own Altar to be burned there.*

<margin>XXIII. At the beginning of the Israelite Republic, Moses performed the High Priesthood extraordinarily, then the right of the priesthood was transferred to the family of Aaron.</margin>
XXIII. From the time that *God formed for himself a Kingdom among the Israelite people*, the *Priesthood* took on an entirely different face. For then the *private right of sacrificing was taken away from individuals, and the public Priesthood was separated from the leadership and transferred by Divine command to* AARON *and his descendants*. The exception was MOSES, who in the desert performed many things as a *Priest* by a unique right. Indeed, he himself initiated Aaron and his sons, by command of the Most Holy Divinity, with the solemn seven-day rites then first instituted. *Leviticus 8.* Nor was he considered merely a *Priest*, but even the *High Priest* <note>original: *Sacerdos summus*, or *Pontifex*</note>. Hence, in the writings of *Philo* <note>Philo of Alexandria (c. 20 BCE – 50 CE), a Jewish philosopher who sought to harmonize the Torah with Greek philosophy.</note> concerning his life, he is called more than once not only *High Priest* <note>original: *ΑΡΧΙΕΡΕΥΣ*</note>, but also *King*, *Legislator*, and *Prophet*. And there exists concerning him in the *Shemot Rabbah* <note>Exodus Rabbah, a midrash (Jewish homiletic commentary) on the book of Exodus.</note> *Section 37*, this tradition, cited by *Selden* <note>John Selden (1584–1654), a renowned English jurist and scholar of Jewish law.</note> in *Succession to the Pontificate, Book I, Chapter I*: *The Rabbis hand down that through all the years the Israelites spent in the desert, MOSES held the office of the High* PRIESTHOOD; *although there have been those whose opinion is that he did so only during the seven days of initiation. Certainly, it is more credible that, once Aaron was initiated, Moses ceased from the functions of the High Priesthood.*

<margin>XXIV. And he defined it with fixed laws.</margin>
XXIV. From 그 that time, all things pertaining to the *Priests* and their function were defined by the most accurate laws. These will now be the primary focus of our consideration: specifically, so that we may attend to those things above all others which prefigured the PRIESTHOOD OF THE MESSIAH through more illustrious <term>types</term> <note>In theology, a "type" is a person, event, or institution in the Old Testament seen as a prophetic symbol of something in the New Testament (the "antitype").</note>. In order to proceed in an orderly fashion through such an abundance of subject matter, we shall distinctly observe these three main Chapters: I. THE PERSONS OF THE PRIESTS. II. THE CONSECRATION. III. THE FUNCTION.

### Book II. Dissertation II.

<margin>
XXV. What was required in the Persons of the Priests.
</margin>

XXV. **In the Persons** of the Priests, four things were required. I. DIGNITY OF BIRTH. II. INTEGRITY OF BODY. III. HOLINESS OF SOUL. IV. CHASTITY OF MARRIAGE.

<margin>
XXVI. The Lineage of the Priests.
</margin>

XXVI. Regarding birth, a Priest had to be: I. From among his brothers, of the ISRAELITE nation. *From the midst of the children of Israel. Exodus 28:1.* II. From the tribe of LEVI. *Deuteronomy 33:8, 10. Of Levi he said: Your Thummim and your Urim belong to the man whom you favor with your kindness. Let them teach your judgments to Jacob, and your law to Israel; let them place incense before your face, and a whole burnt offering upon your altar.* <note>The Urim and Thummim were sacred lots used by the High Priest to determine the will of God in times of crisis.</note> For this reason, even Aaron is referred to as "the Levite." *Exodus 4:14.* And Paul, following Moses, calls it the "Levitical Priesthood." *Hebrews 7:11.* III. From the family of AARON. *Numbers 3:10. Appoint Aaron and his sons, that they may observe their Priesthood: for whatever outsider approaches shall be put to death.* Here "outsider" <note>original: *extraneus*</note> refers not only to one who is not an *Israelite*, but also to one who is not a *Levite*, and indeed even to anyone who is not of the family of Aaron. This is demonstrated by the conspiracy and terrifying end of *Korah* the Levite, who contended for the Priesthood with *Moses* and *Aaron*. *Numbers 16.*

<margin>
XXVII. Samuel, though not a descendant of Aaron, was a Priest by special exception.
</margin>

XXVII. The history of SAMUEL creates no small difficulty: he was not a descendant of Aaron, but a *Levite* from the lineage of that same *Korah* who became famous for such an unhappy fate. *1 Chronicles 6:22, 27, 28.* And yet he is recorded to have sacrificed on several occasions: even for the whole people, with God providing a sign of acceptance for his sacrifice. *1 Samuel 7:9, 10.* Indeed, he did so at God's command. *1 Samuel 16:2, 5.* On this point, both Hebrew and Christian interpreters go in different directions. Some maintain that Samuel did not sacrifice with his own hand, but through Priests to whom that duty had been assigned. But the simplicity of the historical account hardly seems to support this, as there is no trace of any Priest being present except Samuel. Therefore, *Kimchi* <note>David Kimchi (1160–1235) was a renowned medieval Jewish scholar and commentator.</note> considers that there were two exceptions in the Priestly Law: one, if there was no fixed place where sacred rites were performed; for then it was lawful for divine matters to be managed not only in the "High Places" <note>Outdoor shrines, often on hilltops, used for worship before the central Temple was established.</note> but also by private individuals. The other exception was if some Prophet was raised up by God. Thus it was permitted for *Joshua*, for *Elijah*, and now also for *Samuel* to sacrifice. For it was established that Samuel was a Prophet, and the Temple was not yet built; the Ark had no fixed location, and in Shiloh everything was in confusion and disorder. Certainly, by this Prophetic authority Samuel did other things which otherwise do not strictly agree with the prescriptions of the law. For he sacrificed a lamb in Mizpah; and in Ramah, where his house was, he built an altar; and he was accustomed to visit various cities to sacrifice in them. But the deeds of the Prophets are, in a way, privileges <note>In this context, a "privilege" (from the Latin *privilegium*) refers to a special legal exemption or a "private law" granted for a specific case.</note>; for they innovated nothing except by the instinct [of the Spirit...]

### ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND OF CHRIST.

...of the Holy Spirit, who is not bound by the law. Indeed, since it is likely that **Samuel** often sacrificed for the safety of the Commonwealth, most learned men rightly conclude that this privilege of Samuel—namely, that by Divine dispensation he was called to be a Priest from the sons of **Korah** <note>original: *Corachi*; Korah was a Levite but not of the family of Aaron.</note> rather than the line of **Aaron**—was an extraordinary calling placed above the ordinary Priesthood. See, if you will, *Johannes Cloppenburg’s School of Sacrifices, Spicilegium Problem 11.*

<margin>
XXVIII. This example shows that the law regarding the priestly lineage is a matter of positive law.
</margin>

XXVIII. Therefore, Samuel’s Priesthood, whatever its exact nature, certainly had something extraordinary about it. This matter does not seem to be without mystery. Through this exception—whether we call it a dispensation or a departure from the common law regarding the person of the Priest—God demonstrates that the entire law concerning the priestly lineage is a matter of His own discretion <note>original: *juris arbitrarii*; this refers to "positive law"—laws established by divine or human decree—rather than "natural law," which is seen as unchangeable.</note>. Therefore, nothing prevents God from changing it according to His will. In fact, He eventually abolished it entirely when He introduced the better Priesthood according to the order of **Melchizedek**; his Priest is not one whose ancestors served at the altar. <note>Hebrews 7 explains how Christ’s priesthood follows the order of Melchizedek, which does not rely on physical descent from Levi or Aaron.</note> Nevertheless, as long as the Mosaic state remained in force, no one was permitted to the Priesthood by the common law unless they were from the family of Aaron.

<margin>
XXIX. A priest had to be born of a woman of good character.
</margin>

XXIX. Furthermore, even that lineage was not enough for the dignity of one’s birth, unless—as a fourth condition—that descendant of **Aaron** was BORN OF A WOMAN OF GOOD CHARACTER, not a prostitute, not a foreigner, and not a slave. Indeed, specific marriage laws were prescribed for the Priests, which we will discuss shortly. It follows that anyone born from a union forbidden to Priests had to be barred from the Priesthood as "profane." **Josephus** also recorded this in the first book of *Against Apion*: *It is necessary that he who shares in the priesthood should father children with a woman of the same nation.* <note>original Greek: Δεῖ τὸν μετέχοντα τῆς ἱεροσύνης ἐξ ὁμοεθνοῦς γυναικὸς παιδοποιεῖσθαι.</note> Upon this foundation, **Eleazar the Pharisee** built his own outspokenness—or rather, his insolence—when he addressed **John Hyrcanus** <note>Hyrcanus (ruled 134–104 BCE) was a Hasmonean leader who served as both Prince and High Priest.</note> during a generous banquet in this way: "Since you say you desire to hear the truth, if you wish to be righteous, resign from the High Priesthood and be content with the leadership of the people." When Hyrcanus asked for the reason why he should resign the High Priesthood, Eleazar replied: "Because we have heard from our elders that your mother was a captive during the reign of **Antiochus Epiphanes**." <note>Antiochus Epiphanes was the Seleucid king whose persecutions led to the Maccabean Revolt; the law forbade the sons of women taken captive in war from serving as priests, as there was a suspicion they might have been violated.</note> *Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, Book XIII, Chapter XVIII.* That rumor was actually false. But from this speech by the Pharisee, it is easy to see that it was a widely accepted opinion that the son of a captive woman should not be admitted to the High Priestly succession, nor allowed to remain in it.

<margin>
XXX. Genealogical tables of the Priests were carefully preserved.
</margin>

XXX. Furthermore, so that all these matters could be clearly established, and so that no suspicion of such a "taint" <note>original: *inquinamenti*</note> might harm anyone, or a rumor about a tainted family work against one’s priestly duties, the Priests were especially accustomed to record the names of parents, their lineage, and their status in genealogical tables. From these, the purity of birth required for the sacred office was preserved.

### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

...readily asserted. Regarding this matter, see Ezra 2:62 and Nehemiah 7:64. **Josephus** also reminds us in *Against Apion*, Book I, that this was observed not only in Judea but elsewhere. "And we do this," he says, "not only in Judea itself, but wherever a community of our race is found; a lawful care for marriages is maintained by the Priests. I speak of those who live in Egypt and Babylon, and those of the priestly race who are scattered elsewhere throughout the world. For they send the names of their parents and ancestors to Jerusalem to be recorded, along with witnesses to the matter."

<margin>
XXXI. From these records, the Great Sanhedrin judged the family lineage.
</margin>

XXXI. It is notable what **Maimonides** <note>A renowned medieval Jewish scholar and philosopher.</note> teaches in *The Entry into the Sanctuary* <note>original: *Biath Hammikdas*; a section of his legal code, the Mishneh Torah</note>, Chapter XXVI: the Great Sanhedrin <note>The supreme legal and religious council of ancient Israel.</note> held court daily in the Chamber of Hewn Stones <note>original: *Cubiculo cæsorum lapidum*; the meeting place of the Sanhedrin within the Temple complex</note> for the purpose of judging the families of the Priests. Any Priest found to be a stranger to the family of **Aaron**, or whose birth was not sufficiently pure, was ordered to dress in black clothing and cover his head with a black veil, and he would depart from the sanctuary in mourning. However, he whose family was judged legitimate would remain in the sanctuary dressed in white, serving there with his brothers. It is worth considering whether the Lord’s promise in Revelation 3:5 refers to this: *The one who conquers will be clothed thus in white garments, and I will never blot out his name before my Father and before his angels.*

<margin>
XXXII. All these things are transferred to Christ.
</margin>

XXXII. It is not difficult to transfer what we have said to **CHRIST**. For, first: *He is a* MAN *from among* HIS BROTHERS (Hebrews 2:11). *For he who sanctifies—by offering himself as a victim (John 17:19) and pouring out his Spirit—and those who are sanctified are all from one. For this reason, he is not ashamed to call them* BROTHERS. And again in verse 17: *Therefore he had to be made like his* BROTHERS *in every respect, so that he might become a merciful and faithful High Priest in the service of God.* Indeed, He is also an ISRAELITE *from* ISRAELITES. Jeremiah 30:21 says: *And his Prince shall be* FROM HIMSELF, *and his Ruler shall proceed* FROM THE MIDST OF HIM, *whom I will cause to draw near, and he shall approach me.* This "approaching" is the work of the Priests (Exodus 19:22; Ezekiel 40:46, 43:19, 44:13, 15). God adds: *For who is he who would pledge his heart to approach me?* In the Hebrew, it is <note>original: "כי מי הוא זה ערב את לבו" (*Ki mi hu ze arev et libo*)</note>. This can have a twofold meaning. First, *who is he who pledges with his heart*, or *makes his heart sweet*, denoting a voluntary action undertaken with confidence—a confidence, I say, resting on the dignity of the person approaching and his unstained holiness. Second, *who is he who would pledge his heart*, signifying the matter and price of the pledge. For "heart" is the same as "soul." This is what Christ was to give *as a guilt offering* (Isaiah 53:12). All these things were lacking in the ancient Priests. For no one was of such dignity or holiness that he did not himself need expiatory sacrifices (Hebrews 7:27). No one offered himself, but they all offered the blood of another...

# Concerning the Priesthood of Aaron and of Christ.

...the stranger. Hebrews 9:25. Therefore the Messiah, that magnificent and incomparable Priest, is from Israel, coming forth from the midst of his own people. II. However, he is not from the tribe of **LEVI**: so that it might be clear that his Priesthood is of a different order than the Aaronic one. Hebrews 7:13. But he is from the tribe of *Judah*: because he ought to have a Priesthood joined with Royal dignity, after the likeness of **MELCHISEDEK**. Psalm 110:2. III. He was brought forth from the **PUREST LINEAGE**, born of the Royal Virgin, so that he might be free from all stain. Concerning that Birth, the Angel said to Mary in Luke 1:35 <note>The source text cites Luke 2:35, but the quote is from the Annunciation in Luke 1:35.</note>: *The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of you shall be called the Son of God.* But besides that generation from the virgin by which he was made the Son of Man, another generation also belongs to him, entirely Divine and eternal, according to which he is the **SON OF GOD**. Concerning this, Paul spoke most fittingly to our purpose in Hebrews 5:5: *Christ did not glorify himself to be made a High Priest, but he who said to him, "You are my Son, today I have begotten you."* IV. This most pure, and indeed Divine and eternal origin of Christ, has been abundantly **CONFIRMED** by rich testimonies and heavenly assertion. And he himself, while the Father bore witness to him, was clothed in white garments, whose brilliance surpassed snow and light itself. Matthew 17:2, 5.

<margin>
XXXIII. Bodily integrity in a Priest.
</margin>

XXXIII. Thus far we have spoken of the Dignity of Lineage; now let us look at **BODILY INTEGRITY**; which in the Aaronic Priest had to be exquisite, and is accurately described in Leviticus 21:17–21. *Speak to Aaron, saying: "Whosoever of your seed throughout their generations has a bodily blemish, let him not approach to offer the food of his God."* Then so many various bodily defects are enumerated, with this repeated and serious warning added: *“No man of the seed of Aaron the Priest that has a bodily blemish shall come near to offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire: he has a blemish; he shall not come near to offer the food of his God.”* Indeed, the defects enumerated by Moses serve as examples for similar ones, which were reviewed with almost superstitious diligence by the Hebrew Masters <note>The author refers here to the Rabbis of the Talmudic era who codified Jewish law.</note> and divided into three classes. Some defects disqualified both *priests* and *brute animals*, such that the animals could not be properly offered, nor could the priests properly perform the ministry. Others disqualified the *man only*, so that he had to abstain from the sacred ministry. Finally, others did not disqualify for any other reason than that they were displeasing to the observer because of their deformity. Of the first kind, they list fifty. Of the second, ninety. Of the third, only two. In total, 142. He who desires to know these indicated by their specific names should consult *Selden, On Succession to the Pontificate, Book II, Chapter V.* <note>John Selden (1584–1654) was a famous English jurist and scholar of Jewish law; this was a standard reference for 17th-century scholars.</note>

XXXIV. Those suffering from a blemish are removed from sacred duties.

# BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

...as a matter of bad omen, they were rejected by the decree of the law. Those so disqualified thereafter lived in the part of the temple called the Chamber of Wood <note>original: לשכת העצים (*Lishkat HaEtzim*)</note>, which you might call a wood-shed; and there they split the wood that was to be piled upon the altar. Even though they were excluded from the active Priesthood, they nevertheless retained the right to still eat of the sacred meals with the Priests of the division to which they belonged. This was observed from *Josephus* and *Maimonides* by *Cunæus* <note>Petrus Cunaeus (1586–1638) was a Dutch scholar famous for his work on the Hebrew Republic.</note> in his *Of the Hebrew Republic*, Book II, Chapter VIII.

<margin>XXXV. *Christ was whole in both body and soul.*</margin>
XXXV. It is indeed believable that the body of Christ, formed by the Holy Spirit in the womb of the Most Blessed Virgin, was both whole in its members and adorned with all beauty, being venerable to behold. However, we consider that description of Christ left by Nicephorus <note>Nicephorus Callistus Xanthopoulos (c. 1256–1335), a Byzantine church historian.</note>—whom some call the "Father of Fables"—in the last chapter of Book I of his *Ecclesiastical History*, to be unworthy of any real credit. But this physical beauty is the least of it. Most importantly, this strictness of physical perfection signified that the true Priest would be blameless and spotless <note>original Greek: Ἄμωμον καὶ ἄσπιλον (*Amōmon kai aspilon*)</note> (1 Peter 1:19), not so much in body as in soul; one in whom nothing defective, superfluous, or distorted could be found.

<margin>XXXVI. *Holiness of soul in the Priests.*</margin>
XXXVI. If God wished such great care to be taken in examining the wholeness of the body, it is fitting that he required a HOLY DISPOSITION OF SOUL in his Priests all the more. To this pertains the law found in Leviticus 21:6: *They shall be holy to their God, and not profane the name of their God, for they offer the offerings of Jehovah made by fire, the bread of their God, and therefore they shall be holy.* Add to this Isaiah 52:11: *Depart, depart, go out from there, touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of her, purify yourselves, you who bear the vessels of Jehovah.* Because the sons of *Eli* did not observe this properly, but made the office of *Jehovah* contemptible by their crimes, the anger of God burned against them so fiercely that he punished them with a terrible death and stripped all the descendants of Eli of the High Priestly dignity. Therefore, *it is the word of Jehovah, the God of Israel: I had indeed said that your house and the house of your Father should walk before me forever; but now, says Jehovah, far be it from me, for those who honor me I will honor, but those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed.* (1 Samuel 2:30). And on this condition, expressly stipulated, God granted the continuation of the High Priesthood to the family of *Joshua* <note>The High Priest Joshua mentioned in the book of Zechariah.</note> in Zechariah 3:7: Thus says Jehovah, *if you will walk in my ways, and if you will keep my charge, then you shall also judge my house and likewise keep my courts; and I will give you places to walk among these who stand by.*

XXXVII. Furthermore, the Hebrew Teachers observe that there were two crimes in particular which would eternally exclude a Priest from this honorable office, even if he were led by repentance to abstain from them most carefully thereafter: namely, IDOLATRY, and the worship of the true God indeed...

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND CHRIST.

<margin>❦ Three faults in worship in a forbidden place.</margin>
...indeed offered to God, but in a FORBIDDEN PLACE. Regarding this matter, the very learned John Selden <note>John Selden (1584–1654) was an English jurist and scholar of Jewish law.</note> discusses this in his usual thorough manner in *On Succession in the Hebrew Pontificate*, Book II, Chapter 6.

<margin>XXXVIII. All these qualities were exceptional in Christ.</margin>
XXXVIII. There is no doubt that in this regard our Jesus immensely surpasses all the ancient Priests. Paul celebrates His entirely untainted holiness of soul with well-deserved praise in *Hebrews 7:26, 27, 28*. How far He was from IDOLATRY is testified by His own excellent words in *Psalm 16:4*. (We have proven elsewhere that this Psalm is a continuous prayer of the Messiah.) The words of the Psalm, as far as they pertain to our purpose, are as follows: *Their sorrows are multiplied who endow another* <note>original Latin: "Multiplicantur dolores eorum qui Alium dotant"</note>, that is, those who—leaving You, the true God, and Me, the only Mediator—choose another to whom they give themselves, as if to a husband. They do so under this unfair condition: that they do not receive a dowry from him, as is otherwise the custom, but they give a dowry to him. This means they do not receive benefits from him, but instead spend their own resources on his worship. *I will not pour out their drink offerings.* I, the one and supreme High Priest, will not offer drink offerings similar to theirs—idolatrous or hypocritical offerings made of blood, such as the Pagans used to pour out contrary to the law of God. *Nor will I take their names upon my lips.* Not in oaths, nor in daily speech; in short, I will have no dealings with them.

XXXIX. The Lord Jesus also never defiled His worship in a FORBIDDEN PLACE. While the Mosaic administration <note>The author uses the term "Politia Mosaica" to refer to the civil and religious governance of ancient Israel.</note> was in force, He observed the religion of the Temple as was proper. Nevertheless, because the spiritual nature and widely extended greatness of the Messiah's kingdom does not allow the worship of God to remain tied to a single location, Christ wisely warned that the time was approaching *when God should be worshipped neither on Mount Gerizim nor in the Temple of Jerusalem, but everywhere, without distinction of places, in spirit and in truth* (John 4:21, 23, 24). Thus, under the Messiah, it was necessary to fulfill what Isaiah prophesied in chapter 19, verse 19: *There shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt.* And Malachi 1:11: *From the rising of the sun even unto its going down, the name of the Lord shall be great among the nations, and* IN EVERY PLACE *incense and a pure offering shall be offered to Him.*

<margin>XL. Marriage laws enacted for the Priests.</margin>
XL. Finally, CHASTITY IN MARRIAGE was required; the laws for which are distinctly prescribed, first regarding all PRIESTS, and then regarding the HIGH PRIEST. Concerning the former, it is decreed in *Leviticus 21:7*: *They shall not take a woman who is a harlot or profaned; nor shall they take a woman divorced from her husband: for each of them is holy to his God.* Here, it is clear that three types of women are forbidden to Priests: I. <term>אִשָּׁה זֹנָה</term> <note>Hebrew: *Ishah Zonah*, meaning "prostitute" or "harlot".</note>, a *harlot*. II. <term>חֲלָלָה</term> <note>Hebrew: *Chalalah*, referring to a woman profaned or violated.</note>, which the Greek translators <note>The Septuagint writers.</note> render as <term>βεβηλωμένην</term> <note>Greek: *bebelōmenēn*, meaning "profaned".</note>, *profaned*. III. <term>אִשָּׁה גְרוּשָׁה מֵאִישָׁהּ</term> <note>Hebrew: *Ishah Gerushah Me'ishah*, meaning "a woman divorced from her man".</note>, *a woman divorced from her husband.*

# BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

But it is not so obvious how the first two types of women are distinguished from one another. Fagius <note>Paul Fagius (1504–1549) was a noted German Hebraist and Bible scholar.</note> and others think that by **Harlot** one simply understands a woman who prostitutes herself to everyone; by **Profane**, or violated, one understands a woman violated by some chance event. However, the Masters of the Hebrews have a far different notion of these matters. By **Harlot** <note>original Hebrew: *zonah*</note>, they understand:

I. Every woman who is not an **Israelite**, not born of an **Israelite father**, or at least not from an **Israelite mother**. Such as **Proselytes** (converts) and **Freedwomen**.

II. An Israelite woman indeed, but one with whom a man has slept whose marriage is forbidden to her by common law. This includes whether she defiled herself through incestuous intercourse against the prohibition of **Leviticus 18**, or had relations with someone forbidden to marry Israelite women—such as a **Mamzer** <note>a child born of an incestuous or adulterous union</note>, an **Ammonite**, or a **Moabite** (even if they become proselytes), and others of that kind. **Deuteronomy 23.**

III. A woman who slept with a **profane man**, whose marriage would otherwise have been permitted to her. They call a man **profane** <note>original Hebrew: *chalal*</note> who is born from a union forbidden to a Priest by some law specific to the Priestly class or the High Priest.

IV. Finally, a woman who was suspected by a jealous husband, and whose crime—whether real or imagined—remained hidden, and who did not undergo the trial of the bitter water; concerning which see **Numbers 5**. See, if you please, **Maimonides** <note>The preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher and jurist.</note> in *Forbidden Intercourse* <note>original title: *Issurei Biah*</note>, **Chapter 18, Sections 1, 6, 12**.

As for the **Profaned** woman <note>original Hebrew: *chalalah*</note>, it does not denote a lowly prostitute to the Hebrews (as Jerome rendered it), but as the paraphrase of **Uziel** <note>referring to the Targum Pseudo-Jonathan, an Aramaic translation of the Torah</note> has it: **one who is born from those who cannot be lawfully joined to Priests**, such as, for example, the daughter of a widow whom a Priest married.

for the High
Priest.
</margin>
XLI. The marriage law dictated for the High Priest is expressed in these words from **Leviticus 21:13, 14, 15**:
> The Priest who is the highest among his brothers shall take a wife in her Virginity: A widow, or a divorced woman, or a profaned woman, or a harlot, he shall not take: but he shall take a virgin from his own people as a wife. Nor shall he profane his seed among his people: for I am Jehovah his Sanctifier.

The Hebrews maintain that these rules are commanded not only for the High Priest, the successor of Aaron, but also for his deputy, the **Segan** <note>The *Segan* served as the immediate assistant to the High Priest and his substitute if he became ritually unfit</note>, who had to perform his duties on the Day of Atonement if something human happened to him by which he was defiled; as well as for the Priest anointed for war (**Deuteronomy 20:2**). Therefore, to these men, in addition to the three types of women mentioned above, a widow is also forbidden; and it was not lawful for him to take anyone other than a virgin as his wife. And indeed, one **from his own people**. Some interpret this as referring to close kinship, or at least from his own tribes. **Philo** <note>Philo of Alexandria, a Hellenistic Jewish philosopher.</note> certainly, in **Book II on Monarchy**, writes that no one should be betrothed to the High Priest except a virgin who is **a priestess born of priests, so that the bridegroom and bride may be from one house and, in a sense, of the same blood.** <note>original Greek: "ἱέρεια ἐξ ἱερέων, ἵνα ἐκ μιᾶς οἰκίας καὶ τρόπον τινὰ τõ αὐτõ αἵματος ὦσιν νυμφίος τε καὶ νύμφη"</note> **A Priestess from Priests, namely a girl born from a Priest...**

<margin>XLII. How these teach of the chaste loves of Christ and the Church.</margin>
XLII. That is, He inflames the soul with such a chaste and sincere love for Christ that she loves Him no less ardently than one who consecrates the first loves of her virginity to a bridegroom, and she is loved by Him no less than if she were led into the chamber of the most holy bridegroom untouched, knowing nothing of any other love or disgrace. And this is obtained from the blood and Spirit of Christ: *who loved the Church and gave Himself up for her, that He might sanctify her, having cleansed her by the washing of water with the word, that He might present the Church to Himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she might be holy and blameless. Ephesians 5:25, 26, 27.*

XLIII. Thus far we have treated those things which were required by God in the Levitical Priests. Indeed, even other qualities beyond these were required, at least if faith is to be placed in the Hebrew Masters. They hand down the tradition that the High Priest ought to have excelled his brothers in five things: <note>original Hebrew: בחכמה במראה בנוי בכוח בעושר (*be-chokhmah, be-mareh, be-noy, be-koach, be-osher*)</note> **IN WISDOM, IN APPEARANCE, IN BEAUTY, IN STRENGTH, AND IN WEALTH.** *Maimonides in "The Instruments of the Sanctuary," Chapter 5.* <note>Maimonides (1138–1204) was a Sephardic Jewish philosopher and scholar; the work cited is *Kele HaMikdash* from his Mishneh Torah.</note>

### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

They distinguish "appearance" <note>Hebrew: *mar'eh*</note> from "form" <note>Hebrew: *to'ar*</note> in this way: they apply the former term to the elegant build of the body, and the latter to the beauty of its color. They say that both of these were required in the High Priest as a sign of a good character. Yet Maimonides <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204) was a preeminent Jewish scholar whose codification of Jewish law is foundational.</note> is not entirely consistent with himself, since elsewhere, in discussing the High Priest, he demands the highest "faith" instead of "beauty of color." In his commentary on the *Mishnah in Yoma, Chapter 1*, he says: *Among us, it is established as a fundamental principle that it is necessary for the High Priest to yield to no other Priest of his time* **IN WISDOM, FAITH, BEAUTY, WEALTH, AND STRENGTH.** <note>original Hebrew: *be-chokhmah, be-emunah, be-yofi, be-osher, be-khoach*</note> If it should happen that the heir to the High Priesthood were surpassed by perhaps an ordinary Priest in wealth—though not in those other gifts—it was seen as right that such a great man should be enriched by the resources of the other Priests until he became the wealthiest of them all. *Outram, on Sacrifices, Book 1, Chapter 14.* <note>William Outram (1626–1679) was an English theologian known for his scholarly work comparing Jewish and Christian sacrificial systems.</note>

<margin>XLIV. *These qualities are present in Christ in a most distinguished way.*</margin>
XLIV. It is not difficult to transfer these qualities to the High Priest of our profession, Christ; who certainly possesses all excellence above His companions. *Psalm 45:7.* How vividly His ELEGANCE is depicted! *Ibid, verse 2:* **You are much fairer than the children of men** <note>original Hebrew: *yafyafita mi-bene adam*</note>, *grace is poured into your lips; therefore God has blessed you forever.* In STRENGTH He so far surpasses all mortals that He is therefore called the **Mighty One of Jacob**, the **Mighty One of Israel** <note>original Hebrew: *Abir Ya'akov*, *Abiro Yisrael*</note>, *Genesis 49:24 and Isaiah 1:24*; and **His Magnificent One** <note>original Hebrew: *Adiro*</note>, *Jeremiah 30:21.* He is **the one stronger than the strong man**, *Luke 11:22* <note>original Greek: *Ho ischyroteros ischyrou*</note>; and finally, nothing more illustrious could be said than **Mighty God, most robust.** <note>original Hebrew: *El Gibbor*</note> *Isaiah 9:6.* The WEALTH, which He not only possesses Himself but also shares with all His own, is utterly incomparable and inestimable. For it pleased the Father *that in Him all fullness should dwell. Colossians 1:19.* For this reason, Paul praises those *unsearchable riches of Christ. Ephesians 3:8.* In WISDOM, no one can be judged His equal; the twelve-year-old boy displayed incredible examples of it, and with it He so often carried His listeners away into amazement, pouring forth mysteries that had been hidden since the beginning of the world. Indeed, He is that supreme Wisdom celebrated with such magnificent praises by Solomon, the wisest of kings, in his Proverbs. It is His place to say, without any appearance of empty arrogance: *Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding, I have strength. Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness. I cause those who love me to possess substance; finally, I fill their treasuries. Proverbs 8:14, 18, 21.* He also excels in BEAUTY above thousands. *My beloved is white and ruddy, the chief among ten thousand. Song of Solomon 5:10.* <note>The Latin text cites verse 9, but the quote corresponds to verse 10.</note> If "faith" is to be substituted for "beauty of color," He has no equal in this part either: *A merciful and faithful High Priest in things pertaining to God. Hebrews 2:17.*

# On the PRIESTHOOD of AARON and CHRIST.

<margin>XLV. The four ceremonies of consecration.</margin>
XLV. From the consideration of the persons, let us pass to the **CONSECRATION OF THE PRIESTS**, by which they were initiated into their venerable office. According to Divine command, this consisted of four ceremonies: I. **WASHING**. II. **INVESTITURE WITH SACRED GARMENTS**. III. **ANOINTING**. IV. **CERTAIN SACRIFICES**.

<margin>XLVI. Of these, the first is Washing, not taken from the rites of the pagans, but commanded by God.</margin>
XLVI. Regarding the **WASHING**, God's command exists in Exodus 29:4: *“Then you shall command Aaron and his sons to approach the door of the tent of meeting, and you shall wash them with water.”* The fulfillment of this command is found in Leviticus 8:6: *“Moses, therefore, ordering Aaron and his sons to approach, washed them with water.”* This act, while reproaching them for their own impurity (for which they needed washing), simultaneously taught that the holy things of the Lord must be handled only by those who are well-cleansed and purified. It is a very well-known fact that many nations initiated the ministers of their own sacred rites with a similar ritual. However, it does not follow from this that God instituted this purification in imitation of the rites accepted among the ancient pagans <note>The author is arguing against the idea that biblical rituals were merely copied from surrounding "gentile" or polytheistic cultures.</note>. What wisdom or praise is there in the idea that we should think God borrowed the purities and ornaments of His religion from idolaters nearly everywhere? Nature itself dictates that Divine things must be handled cleanly and by the clean. And if symbols are to be used to represent that cleanliness, is much deliberation needed for one to learn that the symbol of washing is the most fitting? since God commended this practice by His own command—as it was already used by the ancient Patriarchs—it was easily accepted by the Israelites; and it is certainly no wonder if other nations were led to the same practice by a natural inclination of the mind.

<margin>XLVII. Which Christ indeed did not need, yet he made use of it.</margin>
XLVII. Our High Priest Jesus, since he was most pure in nature, character, and actions, and untainted by any stain of vice, had no need of washing himself; nevertheless, so that in this part also he might fulfill all righteousness, he saw to it that he was dipped in the sacred bath <note>The author uses the Latin *sacro lavacro tingi*, referring here to the Baptism of Jesus.</note> before the public performance of his office. Matthew 3:13. It is truly no wonder that John initially declined that duty of baptizing Christ, since he recognized himself as the servant and Him as the Lord; he knew himself to be polluted by many stains and Him to be radiantly pure; and therefore he felt he had more need to be washed by Him instead. It is more wonderful that Christ urged it so vehemently, nor does the evidence for the reason he added immediately appear: *“For so it becomes us to fulfill all righteousness.”* I find that interpreters sweat much in explaining these words. I am not displeased by the opinion of those who choose what is simplest: as if the Lord had said, it is necessary for us, in the performance of our office, to offer an example of humility not so much in words as in deeds—both for me, by undergoing your baptism, and for you, by not declining the duty I ask, even though to one reasoning about it, it might seem that it should be done otherwise.

### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

...unless perhaps the interpretation of the illustrious Grotius <note>Hugo Grotius (1583–1645) was a Dutch jurist and theologian whose works on law and scripture were highly influential.</note> is more pleasing: he thinks that **righteousness** <term>original Greek: dikaiosynēn</term> is taken here in its broadest sense, to denote not only **the lawful** <term>original Greek: to nomimon</term>, which is prescribed by law, but also whatever has any regard for equity and honor. For the Law of Moses had prescribed nothing concerning this baptism, and the heavenly command which the Baptist had received pertained properly to repentant sinners. Nevertheless, since Christ was the exemplar of most perfect innocence, even in Him the ceremony—which signified a purpose of preserving innocence—was not empty. Nor could it be more effectively shown how much honor was due to the rites instituted by God than if Christ himself commended their use by his own example.

<margin>XLVIII. The sacred garments of both the Priests and the High Priest.</margin>
XLVIII. The second ceremony by which the Priests were consecrated was the **INVESTITURE WITH SACRED GARMENTS**. Exodus 28:6. These were of two different types: some were common to all Priests, and others were specific to the High Priest. The common ones consisted of four parts, made of the same material of six-fold twisted thread: **Breeches**, a **Tunic**, a **Turban**, and a **Sash**; however, this sash was also embroidered with a woolen weave. For this reason, the Hebrews testify that it had to be removed outside of the time of ministry because of the wool being mixed with linen <note>The Law (Leviticus 19:19) forbade wearing "shaatnez," a mixture of wool and linen, but this was permitted for certain priestly garments during service.</note>. Furthermore, these garments were either "Linen" or "Golden." The Linen garments consisted of the same parts as those of the other Priests, but were made of somewhat more precious material; these served the High Priest only on the sacred Day of Atonement. Leviticus 16:4. The "Golden" garments were so called, not because they were made entirely of gold, but because gold was interwoven in them. Among these, the following especially deserve consideration:

I. The **EPHOD**, a cloak or scapular, which is believed not to have been a robe or a tunic, but a garment hanging only from the shoulders, like a small mantle; yet it was to be bound with a precious belt of gold, and of blue, purple, and fine linen interwoven. On its shoulder-pieces were **TWO STONES**, which Moses calls **Schoham** <note>Hebrew: שֹׁהַם</note>. The Greeks and Philo call them **emeralds** <note>original Greek: smaragdous</note>; Symmachus and Theodotion (according to Jerome) call them **Onyx stones**; and Josephus calls them **Sardonyx**, so as to demonstrate either the color of the stone or its place of origin. The Chaldean translation rendered it as **Beryl**. Abarbanel <note>Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a prominent Jewish statesman and Bible commentator.</note> believes it to be crystal. Whichever of these it may be, it is certain they were precious stones, excellent in size, and suitable for engraving. For the names of the twelve sons of Israel were to be engraved upon them, six on each stone, so that they might be carried by Aaron as a memorial before the Lord.

II. The **BREASTPLATE**, <term>Hebrew: Choschen (חֹשֶׁן)</term> which was to be joined to the ends of the small mantle on the front part. For without this breastplate, the Ephod would have been open. To be inserted into the breastplate were **TWELVE GEMS**, with the names of the tribes engraved upon them, to be carried by Aaron over his heart whenever he entered into the Sanctuary. It is called the "breastplate of judgment" because it was a sign of the judicial power in the High Priest. Inserted into this were also

# On the Priesthood of Aaron and Christ.

URIM & THUMMIM <term>Urim & Thummim: Mysterious objects used by the High Priest to determine the will of God; the names roughly translate to "Lights and Perfections."</term>, concerning which, regarding what they actually were, there are almost as many dissertations as there are flies in the peak of summer heat. We also were compelled to speak of them in our *Egyptian Studies* <note>original: "Aegyptiacis"</note>, to which I have nothing to add now. This much is certain: whatever they were, they pertained to the High Priest’s adornment and signified *Light & Perfection*. It is observed everywhere by the Hebrew scholars that under the Second Temple, that Oracle which was the Most Holy thing in the Breastplate had ceased; nevertheless, so that nothing would be lacking from the High Priest's finery, something similar was expressed by a very skillful imitation, even though there was no practical use for it at that time. ### ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND CHRIST.

Regarding the URIM and THUMMIM—concerning what they actually were—there are almost as many dissertations as there are flies in the peak of summer heat. I too was compelled to speak of them in my *Aegyptiaca* <note>original: "Ægyptiacis"; Witsius’s work comparing Hebrew and Egyptian rituals</note>, to which I now have nothing to add. This much is certain: whatever they were, they belonged to the High Priest’s adornment and signified *Light and Perfection* <note>The Hebrew words Urim and Thummim are generally translated as "Lights" and "Perfections"</note>. It is commonly noted by the Hebrew scholars that during the era of the Second Temple, that most holy Oracle which resided in the Breastplate was missing; nevertheless, so that nothing would be lacking from the High Priest's attire, something similar was crafted through highly skilled imitation even then, though it served no actual purpose at that time. The words of Maimonides <note>A famous 12th-century Jewish philosopher and legal scholar</note> are memorable: *The Vessels of the Sanctuary, Chapter 10.* <note>original Hebrew: עשו בבית שני אורים ותומים כדי להשלים שמנה בגדים ואף עלפי שלא נשאלין בהן</note> *In the time of the Second Temple, they made the Urim and Thummim so that the eight priestly garments would be made complete, even though they never actually consulted that form of the Oracle then.* But what the High Priest then lacked, they hope and pray will be restored through the Messiah. 

III. THE ROBE OF THE EPHOD, or the Tunic, or blue robe, from whose hems hung pomegranates and golden bells.

THE TURBAN, <term>mitznephet</term> <note>Hebrew: מצנפת</note>, the Tiara or linen miter, to which was attached a golden plate with the inscription <term>Holiness to Jehovah</term> <note>original Hebrew: קדש ליהוה</note> HOLINESS TO THE LORD, to be worn by Aaron on his forehead, so that he might bear the guilt of the holy things which the children of Israel had consecrated. ### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

...the belt of the small cloak, and with the turban placed on his head, you shall fit the holy crown upon that turban. The Talmudists <note>Jewish scholars who compiled the Talmud, the body of Jewish civil and ceremonial law</note> add that, before all else, the linen breeches were put on. For God willed His priests to be as modest and reverent as they were covered in body. For this reason, they did not ascend to the altar by steps—lest their nakedness <note>original: "verenda," referring to private parts</note> perhaps be seen—but by a certain ramp. Exodus 20:26. This was in contrast to what was done by the priests of certain profane nations, who exposed those parts which most ought to be hidden in the presence of Peor <note>A reference to Baal-Peor, a Moabite deity associated with licentious rites</note>. Furthermore, for the same reason of modesty, as *Abarbanel* <note>Isaac Abarbanel, a 15th-century Jewish statesman and philosopher</note> rightly observed, while the other sacred garments were placed on Aaron by Moses, Aaron put on the breeches himself in a private place. Indeed, one never reads anywhere of Aaron being dressed in them by Moses. To the breeches was added the *Tunic*, which reached all the way to the feet. Around the tunic was fastened the *Girdle* <note>original: "Balteus"</note>, encircling the body with various wraps; this was done so that the priests would be both more resistant to the cold and more ready for their work. After the Girdle, the *Blue Robe* was put on, with its seventy-two bells and as many pomegranates. To the Robe was added the *Ephod*, the front part of which reached from the armpits to the bottom of the chest, while the back part reached almost to the ankles. Added to this were the *Shoulder-pieces* with their precious stones, as well as the *Breastplate* with its gems. Finally, the High Priest, thus adorned, had the *Turban* placed upon him with its *Golden Plate*.

<margin>
L. They were not to be worn except during sacred ministry.
</margin>

**L.** These sacred garments were not to be worn by the priests, nor by the High Priest, except while they were performing the Sacred Rites. When these were finished, the garments were stored in the storerooms; thus, outside the temple, the Priest did not differ in his style of dress from the rest of the common people. This was the case unless, perhaps, a difficult matter or the public safety required otherwise. This happened when the High Priest Jaddua <note>original: "Jaddos"</note> received Alexander the Great at Jerusalem, accompanied by all the priests, who came forth in their sacred attire, in the prescribed robes <note>original Greek: "ταῖς νομίμοις στολαῖς"</note>.

<margin>
LI. The truth of these things is in Christ.
</margin>

**LI.** The *truth* <note>In this context, the "truth" or "reality" behind the Old Testament symbols</note> of all these symbols is found in Christ. The **LINEN GARMENTS**, which were indeed pure but less grand, signify the bright sincerity of Christ, though stripped of all external pomp, especially when he went to expiate our sins with his own blood. The other **GOLDEN** garments signify the immense glory of the Priest and the Priesthood of Christ, which resides in him as in a fountain, to be shared with those whom he makes into a royal priesthood <note>original Greek: "ἱεράτευμα βασίλειον"; cf. 1 Peter 2:9</note>. Compare Psalm 110:3. Their **MATERIAL** is **VARIED** and **MULTI-COLORED**, but all of it is **PRECIOUS**, noting the variety and richness of the virtues and the manifold grace of God in Christ. Ephesians 2:7, 3:8. The **FORM** of this **MOST SKILLFUL WORK** corresponds to the most exact and orderly practice of the virtues which stood out in Christ; for even that which is established according to his example is praised as the work of a master craftsman’s hands. Song of Solomon 7.

### On the PRIESTHOOD (of AARON AND CHRIST)

**VII. 8.** And so, let these things be said in a general way concerning the mystery of the Priestly garments.

**LII.** Let us descend to the more specific details. The **EPHOD** <note>A shoulder-garment worn by the High Priest</note> with the **ONYX** <note>original Hebrew: "Schoham"</note> stones, upon which were engraved the **NAMES OF THE TWELVE TRIBES OF ISRAEL**, can foreshadow that Christ is clothed in love toward his mystical Israel, and that he carries them upon his shoulders—as in *Isaiah 63:6*—so that he might represent them to God, sustain, support, and rescue them from every evil. Indeed, he carries them like a precious gem, a "treasured possession" <note>original Greek: "περιποίησιν" (peripoiesin), a term for something acquired or preserved as a special treasure; see Isaiah 43:4</note>, a thing by no means to be squandered. And he does this so that he may commend each individual belonging to Israel by name to God, just as he assures them that their names are written in heaven. *Luke 10:20.* Nor are they merely written, but also engraved, *Isaiah 49:16*, by no art or force to be erased or carved out. The **SKILLFULLY WOVEN BAND** <note>The "Cingulum Artificiosum" or Girdle</note> of the Ephod, the likeness of which John saw in the adornment of Christ in *Revelation 1:13*, can denote the readiness, justice, and faith of Christ as he girds himself for the vindication of his people. *Jeremiah 11:5.* The purity of his readiness corresponds to the fine linen <note>original: "Bysso"</note> of the girdle. Its intricate embroidery <note>original: "opus phrygionicum," literally Phrygian work, a common term for high-quality needlework</note> represents the marks and signs of Divine pleasure resting upon it. The **BREASTPLATE OF JUDGMENT** implies that all judgment over His Church belongs to Christ. *Ezekiel 21:32; Psalm 72:1; John 5:27.* The **NAMES OF THE SONS OF ISRAEL** to be carried on the breastplate express the sincere and burning love of Christ toward his chosen ones. In the *Song of Solomon 1:13*, the Bride compares Christ to a bundle of myrrh resting between her breasts; here, Christ compares the faithful to the gems which he carries upon his chest. It is no small thing that the Jasper, the last of the gems in the breastplate, *Exodus 28:20*, is the first in the foundations of the New Jerusalem. *Revelation 21:19.* This is not only because the New Testament begins where the Old Testament ends, but also because Paul—who was from the tribe of Benjamin, represented by the Jasper—was among the principal builders of the New Jerusalem. The **URIM** <note>Hebrew for "Lights"</note> denote the most abundant light of Wisdom, Glory, and Joy. The **THUMMIM** <note>Hebrew for "Perfections"</note> denote the luster of sincerity and the most perfect holiness found in Christ. Likewise, they show that nowhere is it safer or more certain to consult God than through Christ. He has truly restored the heavenly oracles to his Church—oracles that are clearer, more abundant, and regarding matters of greater importance than any ever heard before. He also grants his followers the ability to approach God with confidence and obtains for them the responses of the Spirit, by which they may be taught the way to salvation. Finally, he does not merely provide those things which the Jews admit were missing for their ancestors under the teaching of the Pharisees and scribes—when they were actually destitute of God's presence and consoled themselves only with empty symbols—but he provides far more and greater things than were ever heard of in ancient Israel. The **CHECKERED TUNIC** <note>original: "Tunica tessellata," a tunic woven with a pattern of squares or "eyes"</note> is a symbol of the justice and salvation with which Christ himself is clothed, and with which he clothes his own people.

<note>References: Psalm 132; Isaiah 61:10</note> The **BELLS** <note>original Latin: "Tintinnabula"</note> along with the **POMEGRANATES** <note>original Latin: "Malogranatis"</note> represent the sweet sound of the Gospel of Christ, joined with fruits of the most pleasant color and flavor. <note>Luke 24:19</note> Wherever the Gospel is rightly preached and received, it brings forth fruits worthy of oneself, of God, and of Christ. <note>Colossians 1:6</note> The **TURBAN** <note>original: "Cidaris," the High Priest's head covering</note> made of the whitest fine linen <note>term: "Byssus" (a high-quality ancient flax fabric)</note> represents the most exacting purity of Christ, which he himself possesses as the Head of the elect, displays for the glory of God, and grants to his own people. <note>Zechariah 3:5</note> The **GOLDEN PLATE** <note>original: "Lamina Aurea"</note> with the inscription **HOLINESS TO THE LORD** <note>original: "Sanctitatis Jehovae"</note> signifies the most glorious holiness of Christ, which he shares with his followers in such a way that they may show it even in the smallest details; and through the grace of Christ, that which was once written on the *High Priest's Plate* is now inscribed even on the bells of the horses. <note>Zechariah 14:20</note> By that Plate and Inscription, *Aaron* bore the iniquity of holy things: by which it was taught that not even an offering of gold could be pleasing to God except by the virtue of the High Priest. Religious exercises, even the most distinguished, always suffer from their own imperfections and require expiation and forgiveness, to be obtained through the Priest. <note>1 Peter 2:5</note>

<margin>LIII. Whether John, James, and the rest of the Apostles wore the High Priestly regalia.</margin>

LIII. Since we possess in Christ the very realities that were signified by the array of High Priestly garments, and since Christ shares these things with all those whom he makes a "Royal Priesthood"—those who, having been baptized into him, have also "put on" Christ—we rightly conclude from this that any mystical distinction of external garments is foreign to the simplicity of Christianity. For the Apostle *Paul* taught us that the shadows of things to come give way to the physical reality <note>or substance</note> now present. Hence, not without reason, it may seem strange that the Ancients, by some consensus, hand down traditions concerning *James* and *John*, the disciples of the Lord, as if they, having become Priests of the New Testament, wore the High Priestly regalia. Regarding *James*, *Epiphanius*, *Jerome*, and almost all other ecclesiastical writers relate that he was accustomed to wear the golden plate or thin gold leaf <note>original: "Bracteam auream"</note> on his head. Regarding *John*, *Polycrates* (Bishop of the Ephesians), in that letter which he wrote to *Victor* of Rome and which appears in *Eusebius* (*Ecclesiastical History, Book V, Chapter 24*), speaks in these words: <note>original Greek: "Ἔτι δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἐπὶ τὸ στῆθος τοῦ κυρίου ἀναπεσὼν ὃς ἐγεννήθη ἱερεὺς τὸ πέταλον πεφορηκώς"</note> "Furthermore, John, who reclined upon the breast of the Lord, who also became a priest wearing the Petalon." Now, *Jerome* interprets the word *Petalon* as the **Golden Plate**. From these two examples, *Baronius* <note>a 16th-century Cardinal and historian</note> infers <note>at Year 34, section 289</note> that the other Apostles were also accustomed to use insignia of this kind of dignity. For since this sort of head ornament was once granted by God to the Priests of the ancient law, he argues it is reasonable to believe the same was transferred by Christ to the more ample and perfect Priesthood of the Christian law.

# ON THE PRIESTHOOD OF AARON AND OF CHRIST.

LIV. Furthermore, all these stories—no matter how much consensus they are handed down with by those who lived somewhat shortly after the age of the Apostles—lack even a shadow of plausibility. By what right would the Apostles have worn the insignia of the Levitical Priesthood, when under the ancient law they were excluded from the Priesthood by their very birth, and the Priesthood of the Christian law, whatever that may be, has nothing in common with the Levitical display? Our Lord himself, who is undoubtedly that great High Priest after the order of Melchizedek <note>A biblical figure symbolizing a priesthood distinct from and superior to the hereditary Levitical line</note>, willingly abstained from all external display of clothing and all the insignia of priestly dignity. Is it believable that, after his departure from the earth, he would have wanted his disciples to be crowned with them? Would that be consistent with that profound humility and humble poverty of which the Apostles made a truly sincere profession? What a completely unnecessary, useless, and unedifying metamorphosis this would be: that those who recently walked about as simple men in fishermen’s clothes should now dazzle and turn all eyes toward themselves, shining with miters and gold? Would the Apostles, without cause and without any probable reason, have thus stirred up the hatred of both Jews and Gentiles against themselves? Would the Jews—such great zealots for their Law and Priesthood—have tolerated it? Would they not have reproached the Apostles for it? Would they not have charged them in every forum and tribunal with a massive crime and unspeakable sacrilege? Would they not have attacked them wherever they saw them so adorned? Would the Gentiles have tolerated Jewish men coming from abroad into their cities, displaying such splendid priestly insignia and challenging the priests of their own "idol-madness" <note>original Latin: "idolomaniae"</note> with such pomp? Would even the Christians themselves have tolerated it—those simple and poor people of old, to whom such a display could not fail to be a stumbling block, if they understood what was said by Christ in Luke 17:20: *The kingdom of God does not come with outward show* <note>original Greek: "μετὰ παρατηρήσεως" (meta paratērēseōs), meaning with visible, observable ritual or pomp</note>? These are therefore "Milesian fables" <note>term: "Milesian fables" (fictional, often tall tales), here meaning baseless myths</note> which some of the ancients handed down regarding the priestly ornaments of the Apostles; they were eagerly seized upon by the "parasites of the Pope" so that they might, in whatever way possible, defend the Antichristian pride of their own Pontiff.

<margin>LV. The Priestly Anointing.</margin>
LV. Aaron, having been dressed in his garments, **WAS ANOINTED** with the holy oil. <note>Exodus 29:7; 30:30; Leviticus 8:12</note> For a clearer understanding of this ceremony, three things must be explained: I. The Oil of Anointing. II. The method of anointing. III. The persons to be anointed.

<margin>LVI. The oil of anointing.</margin>
LVI. Regarding the **OIL** of anointing—from what material and in what manner it was to be made—it is accurately set forth in Exodus 30:23 and following. The material is generally called "the most excellent of spices"; more specifically, four types of spices are designated: five hundred weight of "noble" Myrrh <note>The Latin "ingenua" here refers to the high-quality liquid myrrh that flows naturally from the tree</note>; (*so says Junius*: most others prefer "five hundred shekels," for the name of the weight...

### BOOK II. DISSERTATION II.

(It is not clearly expressed by Moses <note>The author refers to the liquid base or specific proportions not explicitly detailed in the biblical text</note>, and is thus supplied in various ways by various authors.) *Two hundred and fifty measures of fragrant cinnamon, the same amount of fragrant cane, and fifty of cassia,* <note>The Latin text reads "quinquaginta" (50), though the Masoretic text of Exodus 30:24 specifies 500 shekels of cassia.</note> *to which must be added a Hin of olive oil. The preparation was to be made according to the art of the perfumer. The Hebrews describe the method as follows: He takes the quantity of each species determined by God and pounds each one separately; then he mixes them all and soaks them in pure, fresh water until their entire essence is extracted. Afterward, he pours in a Hin of olive oil, or twelve Logs (which is the volume held by seventy-two eggs), and cooks it together over a fire until the water evaporates and only the ointment remains. This he preserves in a vessel for posterity.*

<margin>
LVII. *Whether the oil, once prepared by Moses himself, lasted until the times of Josiah.*
</margin>

LVII. It is worthwhile to learn what the Hebrew Masters have handed down regarding this ointment; their opinion was extensively and judiciously explained by Abarbanel <note>Isaac Abarbanel (1437–1508), a prominent Jewish statesman, philosopher, and biblical commentator.</note> in his commentaries on this passage. The summary comes to this: they maintain it was prepared by Moses himself with his own hands, because God said, "YOU TAKE FOR YOURSELF." That is: *You, you yourself, shall take these things and prepare the oil and the anointing, and no other mortal shall dare to prepare it as long as the earth remains.* Because no one else was to make anything like it, they believe that by Divine power—and not without a signal miracle—it was preserved for a thousand years. For if you set aside miracles, by the very nature of things it could not have been possible for it to last so long and suffice for so many uses, as the Rabbis themselves admit. *Did not many miracles occur,* they ask, *with the oil of unction from its beginning to its end? In the beginning, there were no more than twelve Logs; yet with it were anointed the Tabernacle and its vessels, Aaron with his sons for all seven days of their consecration, as well as the succeeding High Priests and Kings. Truly, it was destined to be durable, just as it is said in Exodus 30:31:*

-> "This <note>original Latin: HOC; Hebrew: זה (Zeh)</note> shall be my holy anointing oil throughout your generations." <-

The little word *HOC* <note>The Hebrew word "Zeh"</note> has a value of twelve through Gematria <note>A traditional Jewish system of assigning numerical values to letters; Zayin=7 and He=5, totaling 12</note>, which was the number of Logs. Rabbi Jehuda said: *How much was lost by dripping? How much did the aromatic roots absorb? How much did the heat dissipate?* But they say that Moses, aided by God’s help, secured permanence for this oil, just as he did for the Manna to be kept in the golden Urn; indeed, he even brought it about that this oil converted the surrounding air into its own nature, and thus increased itself. Nor was a mystery lacking in this matter. Namely, that God Almighty established a twofold government among the Israelites: one human, that of the Kings, who are the supreme governors of the people; the other Divine, which is that of the Priests, the ministers of God. He willed both to depend upon the mouth and law of Moses. Therefore, He commanded that Moses himself should prepare the sacred oil to be preserved for the generations of the Israelites, and that he should anoint the first Priests with his own hand, while the Kings were to be anointed with the oil prepared by him—and this usually by a Prophet, the successor of Moses...
